Perform normality test for multiple variables at once

Source: R/ntest.R
ntest.Rd

This function performs a Shapiro-Wilk normality test on multiple variables in a dataframe. It returns the results in a tidy format.

Usage

ntest(df, cols)

Arguments

df

A dataframe containing the data to be tested. It can be supplied directly (ntest(df = mtcars, ...)) or piped into the function (mtcars |> ntest(...)).

cols

<tidy-select> The numeric variables to test for normality, written as unquoted column names, e.g. mpg or c(mpg, disp). Selection helpers such as starts_with() or where(is.numeric) also work.

Value

A tibble with one row per variable and the columns variable, statistic, p.value and method.

Details

Before running any tests, the function checks that df is a dataframe, that all selected columns are numeric, and that each variable has between 3 and 5000 non-missing observations (the range shapiro.test() accepts) and is not constant. If any check fails, the function stops with an error message explaining which variables are affected. It then performs the Shapiro-Wilk test on each variable and returns a formatted dataframe with the test results.

If df is a grouped dataframe, the grouping is ignored and all observations are tested together. Use ntest_by() to test each group separately.

See also

ntest_by() to run normality tests for grouped data

Other assumption tests: ntest_by(), vtest()

Examples

# Test a single variable
ntest(df = mtcars, cols = mpg)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   variable statistic p.value method                     
#>   <chr>        <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>                      
#> 1 mpg          0.948   0.123 Shapiro-Wilk normality test

# Test several variables, piping the data into the function
mtcars |> ntest(c(mpg, disp, hp))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   variable statistic p.value method                     
#>   <chr>        <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>                      
#> 1 mpg          0.948  0.123  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
#> 2 disp         0.920  0.0208 Shapiro-Wilk normality test
#> 3 hp           0.933  0.0488 Shapiro-Wilk normality test
